answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring a bonded history of independently verified work before influence unlocks. Each identity completes random tasks, earns signatures from unrelated reviewers, and faces escalating collateral after failed audits. A velvet ledger records verified work, a lagoon graph exposes correlated behavior, and a nebula quarantine isolates suspicious clusters. Slashing copied histories makes large-scale identity creation uneconomic.
